description.value: A cross-sectional comparison of men with cocaine use disorders and healthy male controls using T1-weighted MRI and voxel-based morphometry to examine gray matter volume as a function of diagnosis, MAOA genotype, and lifetime drug use.

value: we predicted a main effect of addiction where CUD will have reductions in GMV as compared to CON
we hypothesized a gene-by-disease interaction driven mostly by GMV loss in CUD-L
We hypothesize that a model containing both genetic and chronic drug use variables will better explain the predicted morphological deficits in GMV

spans.text: Cross-sectional comparison between 40 CUD and 42 controls

definition.value: Individuals with CUD had GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex, and hippocampus compared with controls.

value: Individuals with CUD had GMV reductions in the left OFC, right DLPFC, temporal cortex, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus compared with controls.

definition.value: Comparing CUD-L with CON-L revealed robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus.

spans.text: Comparing CUD-L with CON-L ( Figure 2 , red), revealed robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus

value: CUD-L had robust GMV reductions in the OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus compared with CON-L. The OFC reduction was part of a significant gene-by-disease interaction, with CUD-L having less GMV than CUD-H and both control groups.

spans.text: CUD-L had significantly less GMV than CUD-H and both CON groups in the left OFC

definition.value: Comparing CUD-H with CON-H revealed GMV reductions in the hippocampus.

spans.text: Comparing CUD-H with CON-H ( Figure 2 , blue) revealed a diagnosis effect of GMV reductions in the hippocampus

value: Comparing CUD-H with CON-H revealed a diagnosis effect of GMV reductions in the hippocampus, but no significant results in the other main-effect regions, including the OFC.

spans.text: Comparing CUD-H with CON-H ( Figure 2 , blue) revealed a diagnosis effect of GMV reductions in the hippocampus; however, this contrast did not produce significant results in any of the other main effect regions including the OFC even at a reduced threshold

definition.value: Multiple regression of GMV with lifetime cocaine use, corrected for age and total brain tissue.

spans.text: In order to understand the contribution of drug use duration in this sample, we conducted multiple regressions in SPM5 of GMV with years of drug use, controlling for age and total brain volume

value: With increasing years of cocaine exposure, GMV reductions were observed in the OFC, DLPFC and hippocampus in the CUD group. Lifetime cocaine use uniquely contributed to variance in OFC GMV and contributed substantially to DLPFC GMV variability.

spans.text: with increasing years of cocaine exposure, there were more volume reductions in the OFC (r = −.44, P = .003), DLPFC (r = −.41, P = .008) and hippocampus (r = −.46, P = .003)

definition.value: Multiple regression of GMV with lifetime alcohol use, corrected for age and total brain tissue.

spans.text: Lifetime years of alcohol and cigarette use was evaluated in the whole sample (N=82)

value: Lifetime alcohol use was associated with GMV reductions in the DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus. Alcohol use was the major contributor to GMV deficits in the DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus and contributed unique variance beyond genotype and other variables, especially in the hippocampus.

spans.text: Lifetime alcohol use was the major contributor of GMV deficit in the DLPFC, temporal cortex and hippocampus of CUD

definition.value: Multiple regression of GMV with lifetime cigarette use, corrected for age and total brain tissue.

spans.text: Lifetime years of alcohol and cigarette use was evaluated in the whole sample (N=82)

value: Lifetime cigarette smoking was associated with GMV reductions in the hippocampus.

spans.text: a similar pattern of results was obtained in the CUD group with lifetime alcohol (all r from −.34 to −.65, P <.001) and with cigarette smoking (all r from −.31 to −.52, P <.0001 )
